title.narrative: ROAS: Japan Village Project (Phase II) Emergency Support to Returnees in Northern Iraq – Addressing Housing Crise due to IDPs Camps Closure and Climate Change Challenges

description.narrative:
The project aims to strengthen social stabilization and peace targeting the returnees taking into account the durable solutions, in response to IDPs Camps Closure, Housing Crise, and Deteriorating Climate Change through (a) construction of social housing units, including partnership activities with Japanese private entities for such as water, sanitation and hygiene facility (WASH sector), library (education sector), and climate change by incorporating their innovative approaches, and (b) relevant vocational training and public outreach campaign programme.
This project is the second phase of the Japan Village Project, aims to expand the housing capacity and further enhance public infrastructure to accommodate the growing needs of returnees. The key component of this phase is the construction of an additional residential building within the premises provided by the Mosul Municipality for the Japan Village Project. This expansion aligns with the long-term vision of creating a well-structured, sustainable, and integrated housing complex that fosters community stability and resilience.
The project will be designed and implemented in close coordination with the Government of Iraq and the local authorities both at the governorate and the municipality level, including the municipality of Mosul and Governorate of Ninewa.
The project is fully in line with relevant government policies, including General Framework Document of the National Plan for the Reconstruction and Development of the Provinces Affected by the Terrorist and Military Operations published by the Ministry of Planning, as well as the Housing Reconstruction Strategy in Governorates affected by Terrorism and Military Operations endorsed by the Council of Ministers. The project is also consistent with the aims of the National Framework for Reconstruction and Development, and the principles of the National Development Plan, particularly in relation to the Housing and Accommodation Sector.
The project aims to make synergies and maximize impact together with other projects in Mosul area supported by other donors or implemented by other organizations within the Iraqi National Plan for Displacement and the Inter-Agency Durable Solutions Strategic and Operational Framework. Both of them are used to classify needs and interventions that have been identified at the local level through the Mosul Joint Coordination Forum (JCF). For this purpose, UN-Habitat will continue to closely collaborate with the Mosul Joint Coordination Forum (JCF) and also the Durable Solutions Technical Working Group (DSTWG) which are formed by UN agencies, I-NGOs, and etc. in Iraq.
The proposed project aims to stimulate local economy which has been further exacerbated by socio-economic consequences of COVID-19 and the economic impact of the on-going wars in Gaza and Ukraine by contracting local construction companies which will provide employment opportunities for local community members, including unemployed young women and men, as well as graduates of vocational trainings of the proposed project and locally procuring necessary goods for construction of social housing units and public infrastructure.
The project contributes to strengthen the humanitarian-development-peace nexus as it is a combination of humanitarian assistance, providing safe shelter and access to essential needs to vulnerable returnees, as well as assistance to support self-reliance and dignity of returnees through vocational training and provision of employment opportunities. The project will help returnees to become less dependent on humanitarian assistance through stronger social cohesion and improved livelihoods.
The project will contribute to empower women and girls in the project site and neighborhoods by engaging them to plan and design phases and implement project activities through community consultation meetings. The project will also conduct the capacity development and awareness-raising in response to the negative impact on the climate change specifically prioritizing women and girls to enhance their self-reliance.
Main Expected Accomplishment:
Outcome 1: Living conditions in the targeted communities/neighborhoods are improved through construction of social housing units, including partnership activities with Japanese private entities for such as water, sanitation and hygiene facility (WASH sector), library (education sector), and climate change by incorporating their innovative approaches with environmentally friendly manners. Disability-inclusive development is also to be taken into account as an essential condition for a sustainable future which is in line with the UN disability inclusion strategy to accelerate peace and security, human rights, and development.
Output 1-1: Social housing units are constructed in the site to accommodate 24 households of housing units with approximately 170 beneficiaries.
